_note: RE-CALIBRATED 2026-07-27 (night) after the pilot session in which Samuel could not enrol and cross-identity grants were observed. Method: every palm frame the live deployment recorded (pulled from Azure Files), each person's template rebuilt from their most recent enrolment session exactly as production stores it (3 anchors), scored leave-one-out. EVIDENCE — GENUINE, same session as enrolment: 0.8539 / 0.9010 / 0.9526 / 0.9860 (min 0.8539). GENUINE, 12 h later: 0.7431. GENUINE, ~3 days later: 0.6076-0.7064 (Edwina 0.6783) — i.e. cross-day probes fall INTO the impostor range and cannot be separated by any threshold. IMPOSTOR, 88 cross-identity pairs: max 0.6933, mean 0.4381. The old 0.65 sat BELOW that impostor ceiling and produced 2 wrong-person grants in the sweep. 0.75 clears the worst observed impostor by 0.057 and still accepts every same-session genuine (4/4), giving ZERO wrong-person grants across all 110 scored pairs. identify_margin 0.05 -> 0.10: the margin alone removes the remaining false accepts at any threshold, and same-session genuines beat their runner-up by far more than 0.10. CONSEQUENCE, by design: a person enrolled more than ~12 h earlier will be refused and must re-enrol. That is the deliberate trade — a refusal is recoverable, admitting the wrong person is not. dupe_threshold stays 0.80, above verify, because refusing an enrolment is a stronger claim than refusing a verify (worst cross-person enrol score observed: 0.7078). Keep in sync with android Config.kt PalmConfig.MATCH_THRESHOLD. Re-run scratch/palm_clean.py-style leave-one-out as enrolments grow; revisit once cross-session robustness improves (more diverse anchors, or a domain-adapted encoder).
